entities.name: PMID:25096191
observations: Lee et al. reported that SIRT1 is critical for maintenance and oncogenic transformation of neural stem cells.
SIRT1 was reported as required for survival and tumorigenicity of F3.Ras.CNSCs and glioma stem cells, but not U87 glioma cells.
The paper attributes these effects to p53-dependent tumor surveillance.

entities.name: SIRT1
observations: SIRT1 was reported to support oncogenic transformation of F3.Ras.CNSCs and survival/tumorigenicity of F3.Ras.CNSCs and glioma stem cells.
The reported dependence was context-specific because U87 glioma cells were not SIRT1-dependent.
The proposed mechanism is suppression of p53-dependent tumor surveillance.

entities.name: TP53
observations: The primary paper interprets SIRT1 effects through p53-dependent tumor surveillance.
PubTator annotations identify a negative-correlation relation between SIRT1 and TP53 in the paper.
Detailed p53 rescue or epistasis experiments could not be verified from the accessible record.

entities.name: F3.Ras.CNSCs
observations: F3.Ras.CNSCs are cancerous neural stem cells generated from immortalized human neural stem cells after a single oncogenic stimulation and reported to form glial tumors in vivo.
SIRT1 was reported as required for their survival and tumorigenicity.

entities.name: Glioma stem cells
observations: Glioma stem cells were used as cancer cells retaining neural stemness.
Their survival and tumorigenicity were reported to require SIRT1.

entities.name: U87
observations: U87 glioma cells were used as a comparator and were reported not to depend on SIRT1 for survival or tumorigenicity.
